summary: A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave Thioridazine high risk scores for heart and liver harm [M]. The drug was pulled from the worldwide market starting in 2005 due to heart harm, and it carries the FDA's strongest warning for life-threatening irregular heartbeats, sudden death, and infectious disease [3][4][7]. Additionally, warning labels note that elderly patients with dementia-related mental health issues face a higher risk of death when taking this type of drug [7].
